item.description: Bob Frid-Imagn Images Cutter Gauthier’s simple statement after scoring another hat trick appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The NHL has a few players who are making quite the impact early in the 2026-27 NHL season. However, they may not be a more prolific goal scorer in the NHL right now than Anaheim Ducks forward Cutter Gauthier. He proved why on Sunday night against the Pittsburgh Penguins. Gauthier scored a hat trick on Sunday to help the Ducks claim a 5-2 win. The former first-round pick now has three hat tricks in his last five games. On Sunday, he sent a pretty straightforward warning to the rest of the NHL after the win over Pittsburgh. “I’m just shooting the puck and they’re going in, so I’m just going to keep shooting it,” the young star said, via NHL.com. Gauthier became the fourth player in Ducks history to score three hat tricks in a season. He joins Corey Perry, Teemu Selanne, and teammate Frank Vatrano in that exclusive club. “He’s so natural. You see those shots going five-hole, like that’s a goal-scorer’s goal,” teammate Mikael Granlund said of Gauthier, via NHL.com. “It’s impressive and it’s fun to watch.” The Ducks have something special in Gauthier, without a doubt. item.title: Gauff opens WTA Finals with gritty win over Pegula
item.description: Coco Gauff is the number four seed at the WTA Finals [Getty Images] Coco Gauff battled to a three-set victory over fellow American Jessica Pegula as she made a winning start to the WTA Finals. Gauff, the 2024 champion, demonstrated resilience and superb athleticism to overcome 2023 runner-up Pegula 6-4 6-7 (5-7) 6-2 at Indian Wells in California. Gauff - at 22, the youngest player to appear at five consecutive WTA Finals since Martina Hingis in 2000 - last competed at the China Open in early October. "I'm really proud of myself for this one," she said. "To play a tournament like this with no preparation is something I've never done in my career, but I'm just really happy to get through. "It was a tough match. I was having a lot of fun." Gauff has won only one title in 2026, when she beat Pegula in the Cincinnati Open final in August. Pegula, 32, has won titles in Dubai and Charleston and reached the semi-finals of the Australian Open and US Open. She is only four wins behind Rybakina's tour-leading 54 this season, despite playing only one match since the US Open ended in September. "Jess is an incredible player. We always go back and forth," Gauff said. "Today the key was just trying to be aggressive, but I also had to run a lot. "My shoes are pretty torn up now. Some of my shoes are somewhere on the court there. So I'll have to change shoes tomorrow." WTA chair apologises to Pegula for airing of 'diva' comment In the next round Gauff will face Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova, who beat Marta Kostyuk 6-2 6-4 in the opening match of the Finals. Czech 21-year-old Noskova won all four of her break points against the Ukrainian, who was given a late call-up after world number one Elena Rybakina withdrew on Saturday because of illness. The Finals feature the top eight players this season. Against Pegula, Gauff recovered from three break points down to hold for a 5-4 lead in the first set before breaking Pegula in the following game. Pegula won each of Gauff's first three service games in the second set as she raced into a 5-1 lead, but Gauff took the next three games. Pegula, who wasted three set points when serving at 5-4, unleashed a yell of frustration and slammed her racquet into the ground after missing two break points in the following game. Pegula survived match point on her own serve to force - then win - a tie-break. But Gauff dominated the deciding set, comfortably winning the first three games before converting a third match point and letting out an emotional roar. item.title: Jose Mourinho surpasses Pep Guardiola to set historic La Liga record amid Real Madrid resurgence
item.description: Jose Mourinho surpasses Pep Guardiola to set historic La Liga record amid Real Madrid resurgence Jose Mourinho’s second stint at Real Madrid did not start in the best possible fashion, with the manager taking some time to get his team together. It did not help that Los Blancos signed a number of new players during the summer transfer window who had to be carefully integrated into the squad. However, after the first international break, the team came into their own and have now secured eight consecutive victories across all competitions. The latest victory at Mestalla helped Jose Mourinho achieve a remarkable milestone. The 63-year-old now boasts the highest winning percentage of any manager in La Liga . Mourinho surpasses Guardiola in historic ranking Mourinho has reached the summit of an esteemed list of managers who have overseen at least 100 matches in the league. Across his two spells in the Spanish capital, Mourinho has recorded an impressive 97 victories in 126 La Liga encounters. This gives him a remarkable win percentage of 77%, which sees him surpass Pep Guardiola, who managed 76.3% during his time at Barcelona. Mourinho and Pep Guardiola had a longstanding managerial rivalry during the Portuguese manager’s first stint at the club. Former Real Madrid managers Carlo Ancelotti and Zinedine Zidane occupy third and fifth places respectively, with winning percentages of 71.1% and 67.8%. Rounding out the top five is Xavi Hernandez, who sits fourth on the list with 69.6%. Barcelona’s current manager, Hansi Flick, boasts a higher percentage of 79.3% but does not make the list, having managed only 87 league matches. Mourinho rediscovering his winning formula at Real Madrid The achievement is quite remarkable considering the kind of start Mourinho had to his second spell at Madrid. However, the team have clicked and are now performing at a very high level. Mourinho has made some tactical tweaks that have made the team much stronger. Jose Mourinho has done exceedingly well in the last couple of months at Real Madrid. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) The team have scored 24 goals during their eight-game winning streak, and the defensive commitment of attacking players has improved considerably. Mourinho is increasingly succeeding in making the team a more cohesive unit rather than a group of individuals. The Portuguese manager previously guided Madrid to the historic 100-point La Liga title during the 2011/12 campaign, breaking Barcelona’s domestic dominance under Guardiola. He is now tasked with the same kind of challenge, with Hansi Flick’s Barça having won the last two league titles. It remains to be seen whether Los Blancos can maintain this momentum after the international break.

item.title: INTERVIEW: Dortmund hero Owomoyela anticipates "intense" renewed Revierderby rivalry with Schalke 04
item.description: INTERVIEW: Dortmund hero Owomoyela anticipates "intense" renewed Revierderby rivalry with Schalke 04 Borussia Dortmund icon Patrick Owomoyela senses the Revierderby with arch rivals FC Schalke 04 may take time to regain its overall importance. This, he feels, is largely due to the Gelsenkirchen side’s three-year absence from the Bundesliga and their waining dominance. “It is [a big game], but it hasn’t been there for so long now that people [from Dortmund and Schalke] were urging for it. However, it’s still something that’s far away,” Owomoyela told Bulinews.com and others at a media round table event in Munich last week. “Even when they [Schalke] were still in the Bundesliga [most recently], it was still important for the fans, but it wasn’t as important for the outcome of the season compared to playing against Bayern. “In my time, it was [very important]. Firstly, we were both competing for the championship, so the derby was the biggest game. You could lose all the games but if you won those two [against Schalke] it was a perfect season [for fans]. “At least it felt that way, but now it has changed. Now Bayern is the biggest rival. The fans are happy that it [the Revierderby] is back, but it’s not shining as brightly as it did during my years as a player. “I mean, when we come to within two weeks or a week out from the game, then I am sure my feelings will change,” the Hamburg native said with a smile, casting his thoughts forward to the clubs’ first meeting in early December. When asked if he would like to see the Royal Blues return to a level akin to the era of the 2010s which saw regular European football, the 46-year-old welcomed the idea. He reckons it would give the Ruhrpott’s heavyweight clash some added spice. “It would be fantastic if it wasn’t just [an important fixture] for the pure rivalry, but also an important game for the [outcome of the] season. That would add to the importance of it and that would be something [special]. “It will be a fantastic game, it will be intense and a hard-fought fight, I’m sure. But of course [Schalke becoming more successful] would add a special ingredient to this derby for sure,” he said ahead of the early December encounter.

item.title: Packers & Bengals win in style - NFL week nine
item.description: The Green Bay Packers now have a 6-3 record while the Cincinnati Bengals are 6-2 [Getty Images] The potential Super Bowl contenders are starting to emerge in the NFL with the regular season having reached its halfway point this weekend. The San Francisco 49ers have the league's best record after winning on Sunday and will be joined on 7-1 by either the Buffalo Bills or Minnesota Vikings - provided they do not have a tie in Monday's game. The Chicago Bears and Denver Broncos both ground out hard-fought wins to improve to 7-2 heading into their bye weeks. The Cincinnati Bengals put on a show as the NFL's international series continued while the Green Bay Packers outclassed one of last season's Super Bowl teams. Here are the top stories from week nine in the NFL. Broncos claim NFL record After winning at defending champions Seattle last week, Chicago looked set for another impressive victory as they charged into a 14-0 lead against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Sunday's primetime game. Bears quarterback Caleb Williams then threw a career-high four interceptions before the Bucs drew level with three minutes remaining. But Williams managed to lead the hosts into field-goal range, with Cairo Santos making a 38-yard kick as time expired to beat the Bucs 27-24 for Chicago's fourth straight win. The Bears are now second in the NFC North, the only division in which all four teams have a winning record, but will go top if the Vikings lose to the Bills on Monday. Denver are top of the AFC West after they scored two touchdowns in the final quarter and sacked Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young with just over a minute left to clinch a 26-21 road win. Not only did it extend the Broncos' winning run to five but was their 16th straight win in one-score games in the regular season - a new NFL record. Bengals put on a show in Spain Touchdown scorers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins entertained the Spanish crowd with a matador and bull celebration [Getty Images] Joe Burrow attended Milan fashion week this summer and modelled in Paris in 2024, but this week he visited Madrid to play his first international game. The Cincinnati Bengals quarterback vowed to put on a show at the Bernabeu Stadium in the seventh of a record nine international games this season, and the Bengals did just that as they beat the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 to go 6-2. After being involved in six touchdowns last week, Burrow played a part in another four in Spain. The 29-year-old completed 24 of his 29 passes for 271 yards to cement himself as a contender for his first Most Valuable Player award. Ja'Marr Chase had a season-high 155 receiving yards as the Bengals scored more than 30 points for a fourth straight game – tying a team record. The Bengals are now 6-2 and joint-top of the AFC North with the Pittsburgh Steelers, who they face in next Sunday's primetime game. item.title: LSU’s Lane Kiffin Flips Texas-Based Recruit From Kansas After Loss
item.description: BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 17: Head coach Lane Kiffin of the LSU Tigers reacts during the first half of a game against the Mississippi State Bulldogs at Tiger Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Tyler Kaufman/Getty Images) Getty LEXINGTON, KENTUCKY - OCTOBER 10: Lane Kiffin the head coach of the LSU Tigers gives instructions to his team against the Kentucky Wildcats at Kroger Field on October 10, 2026 in Lexington, Kentucky. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) Getty Lane Kiffin and the LSU Tigers lost on Saturday to the Alabama Crimson Tide. On Sunday, though, Kiffin and LSU picked up a solid recruiting win in getting a flip to their side. The news emerged from Rivals in a report on Sunday, and the details are right here. LSU Flips Recruit Getty LEXINGTON, KENTUCKY – OCTOBER 10: Lane Kiffin the head coach of the LSU Tigers gives instructions to his team against the Kentucky Wildcats at Kroger Field on October 10, 2026 in Lexington, Kentucky. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) LSU has a new linebacker commitment: Ja’Marquis Hudson. Hudson was committed to Kansas, and he plays his high school ball in Texas at Port Arthur Memorial, but he is now a Tigers commit. Rivals reports that Hudson took a second visit to LSU and is now going to come play for the Tigers. “LSU has been watching my senior season and I’m excited about being back in my home state,” Hudson told Rivals . “I’ve been watching LSU since I was a kid, and all of my family are naturally big fans of the Tigers being from Louisiana, so it’s just great ties and it fits perfectly.” Rivals details that Hudson’s mother wanted to attend LSU herself before her family moved to Texas. Now, Ja’Marquis Hudson gets to bring the family roots back to Louisiana. “The culture and how dedicated everyone is to participating in the culture,” Hudson told Rivals. “… I feel football teams feed off stuff like that as motivation.” Rivals details that Hudson went to LSU’s home game against Mississippi State earlier this season and then was back in town on Saturday. Evidently, the loss to Alabama didn’t slow his interest in ending up at LSU. What to Know About Ja’Marquis Hudson According to Rivals, Hudson is the No. 580 overall prospect in the Class of 2027. He’s the No. 44 linebacker recruit in his class nationally, as well as the No. 73 recruit in the state of Texas. Hudson is listed at 6-foot-3 and 200 pounds and also runs track — in a state that has some of the country’s fastest track athletes. It’s worth noting that this recruiting loss is a tough one for Kansas — Hudson was set to be one of their best gets in the Class of 2027. Instead, it’s LSU that has swooped in pretty late to get a talented new player coming their way. They’ll just have to make sure they get Hudson to sign on signing day. item.description: Crystal Palace FC v Liverpool - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Andoni Iraola has confessed that Liverpool desperately required their 3-1 Premier League victory over Crystal Palace to arrest a worrying slump in form. The Reds arrived at Selhurst Park under significant pressure following a bruising week that saw them suffer back-to-back losses on both domestic and European fronts. Returning to winning ways Goals from Alexis Mac Allister, Florian Wirtz, and Alexander Isak secured a vital three points for the visitors in south London . Liverpool took a narrow lead into the break following a closely contested opening period, largely thanks to a crucial save from Alisson. Following the restart, the Reds assumed complete control against a stubborn Palace side. After struggling with their final ball against an initial defensive block, the visitors quickly capitalised on the spaces that opened up once they established their advantage. Iraola analyses Selhurst Park triumph Iraola expressed his relief at navigating a tricky away fixture following their recent defeat to Fenerbahce. "We needed this win, definitely, especially after the defeat the other day in Turkey," the manager explained. "This was another away game and we need to find ways to win in this kind of stadium. I'm very pleased for the three points." Breaking down the tactical shift, he added: "In the first half the game was quite open, chances for both teams and we had a save from Alisson that is key for us. The first goal was important, to go 1-0 up by half-time. In the second half we defended much better, we controlled much better the game. "In the second half when we are ahead, we have spaces to attack and it becomes much easier. The first half was different, they had a lower block. We found good positions between the lines but we weren't giving the last pass properly." Szoboszlai fitness sparks fresh fears The vital victory was ultimately marred by a potential setback for Dominik Szoboszlai. Making his first league start since recovering from a hamstring issue, the Hungarian midfielder picked up a first-half knock that has now jeopardised his impending international commitments. "Dom definitely wasn't 100 per cent in the second half," Iraola revealed. "The last thing we need now is to lose players in the international games. In the last international break we lost three very important players in Alex, Cody [Gakpo] and Dom." Detailing the specific issue, he added: "I think Dom extended the knee a little bit. item.title: Mike Vrabel refuses to sugarcoat Patriots’ disastrous home defeat against Packers
item.description: Photo by Danielle Parhizkaran/The Boston Globe via Getty Images Mike Vrabel offered a brutally honest assessment after the New England Patriots suffered a 45-27 defeat to the Green Bay Packers at home, admitting his team had been thoroughly outplayed. The Patriots entered the Week 9 meeting with confidence after coming from behind to beat the Miami Dolphins on the road. They were also celebrating their 2016 championship team in front of their home supporters. However, it was the Packers who left Foxborough with plenty to celebrate after delivering a dominant performance on both sides of the ball. Mike Vrabel demands more from Christian Gonzalez after New England Patriots defeat Vrabel did not attempt to hide his frustration when discussing the result. Speaking to reporters , the Patriots head coach said: “We got our a***** kicked. There’s no two ways about it.” Jordan Love was at the heart of Green Bay’s impressive display, completing 23 of 29 passes for 372 yards and three touchdowns without throwing an interception. He also opened the scoring with a 13-yard rushing touchdown. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden caused plenty of problems for New England’s secondary. Watson finished with seven receptions for 171 yards and a touchdown while Golden recorded 10 catches for 164 yards and another score. The Patriots also struggled to protect Drake Maye from Green Bay’s defence. Xavier McKinney intercepted the quarterback twice while Evan Williams added another interception. Vrabel also addressed the performance of Christian Gonzalez, making it clear that the cornerback must deliver more for the team. “When your best players don’t play good, you don’t have much of a chance in this league,” Vrabel said, per WEEI. “So we expect a lot more; he expects a lot more. We need more from him and everybody else. It wasn’t just him.” Gonzalez accepted responsibility for his display, admitting: “They got the best of me today…I had a bad game.” According to Pro Football Focus figures shared by Alex Barth, opponents completed 10 of 11 passes when targeting Gonzalez, gaining 187 yards and a touchdown. The cornerback recorded just one pass breakup. The result leaves New England with a 5-4 record heading into another difficult assignment against the Detroit Lions in Week 10. Vrabel also acknowledged that responsibility for the defeat starts with him, making clear that the Patriots have plenty to address before their next outing. item.description: Seventh-tier Wimborne are one of nine non-league teams still fighting in the FA Cup ahead of the second-round draw. However, the victory came at a cost. All-Pro wide receiver Puka Nacua hurt his knee on the Rams’ final offensive snap of the game and is set to undergo an MRI on Monday, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter and NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo. The good news is the Rams don’t believe Nacua tore his ACL. The bad news? One well-known sports doctor is worried about a different ligament in the same knee. Such an injury could sideline him for a significant period of time. Sports Doctor Worried About Puka Nacua’s PCL Getty There’s serious concern for Los Angeles Rams WR Puka Nacua after he was injured against the Commanders With under two minutes left, Nacua took a hard hit. He got up and walked off the field on his own, but the injury was flagged after the game. It put a damper on what was otherwise a monster day for Nacua, who finished with 14 catches for 150 yards and a touchdown. Former NFL team doctor David Chao reviewed the video and agreed with the early reports that it’s unlikely an ACL tear. Still, he has another concern. “Based on video, I agree that an ACL tear is unlikely for Puka Nacua,” Chao posted on X . “My concern is a possible aggravation of the PCL injury in the same knee that sidelined him for five games in 2024. item.description: Late Buchanan and Carlos Romero goals give Villarreal 2-0 win over Getafe La Liga · Regular Season – 12 · 8 Nov 2026 Villarreal 2 – 0 Getafe Tajon Buchanan 80' Carlos Romero 90+1' Half-time 0–0 · Venue: Estadio de la Cerámica · Referee: Carlos Muñiz Muñoz Villarreal ended a two-game losing run on Sunday, 8 November, with a home win over Getafe in matchday 12 of LaLiga . Both goals came in the final 10 minutes at the Estadio de la Cerámica. Tajon Buchanan scored first and Carlos Romero added the second in stoppage time. Iñigo Pérez’s side came into the game after a 0-1 league defeat to Espanyol and a 0-6 loss to Paris Saint-Germain. Their expected goals figure of 2.38, against 0.68 for the visitors, reflected how one-sided the attacking play was. Getafe picked up the first two bookings. Mario Martín was cautioned in the 32nd minute and Nemanja Gudelj in the 62nd, both for fouls. Getafe committed 13 fouls in total, and Villarreal committed 6. Santi Comesaña and Renato Veiga were then booked for the home side in the 67th and 76th minutes. The breakthrough came in the 80th minute. Norris jumped off the top step, and tried to do his signature move, where he uncorks the champagne bottle by bashing it into the ground. Except that, not for the first time, the force of his jump pushed things too far, and he smashed the bottle. Then, holding up the shattered top to the crowd below, he stepped backwards and inadvertently put the side of his head into the sparkles blowing up from the fireworks on the front of the platform. Red Bull drivers Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar showed no pity, and proceeded to drench him with the contents of their bottles. In any case, Norris was fine, McLaren team principal Andrea Stella confirmed shortly afterwards, and the Briton showed no ill effects in his post-race interviews. It was, he said, "one of the hardest races of the year in terms of focus needed every lap and therefore one of the best". Norris wins gripping race after Antonelli and Russell errors Norris brilliant in wet & Verstappen recovery extraordinary - driver ratings Interlagos did what it often can, and threw everything at the drivers. The race started on a wet track, which dried progressively. There was more rain at the end. Through it all, Norris was virtually impeccable. He made new world champion Kimi Antonelli look fallible for pretty much the first time all year, and then fended off what at one point was threatening to be one of those days when Verstappen appears to have descended from the Gods. It says a lot for Norris' performance that it overshadowed Verstappen's drive from 21st on the grid to finish second. Actually, perhaps the race had also started with a small blemish from the man who has had to hand his title of world champion to Antonelli this year without ever really being able to defend it. item.title: England make massive step up in Australia victory
item.description: [BBC] In his latest BBC Sport column, England World Cup winner Matt Dawson reflects on an impressive 45-22 win for Steve Borthwick's side against Australia in the Nations Championship on Sunday. Beating Australia with their record points tally against the Wallabies was a very positive way for England to start the autumn series, given the break they have had and how the beginning of the year went. England were very accurate, very disciplined, creative and genuinely did not give Australia a sniff. Before the game, I was expecting Australia to provide much more of a stern test. Some people might be a bit too critical of Australia, saying they did not turn up, but I think it edges more towards how well England played than how average Australia were. I am not saying by any stretch that it was the perfect performance but, all in all, it was a massive step up from the Six Nations and even from the Nations Championship games in the summer. Intensity, accuracy and discipline in abundance A couple of days before the Australia game, Jamie George said the England team had been galvanised by a newspaper article which claimed the end of their summer tour had been marked by player unrest over head coach Borthwick's leadership. When you are inside those international camps, you are very deliberate in staying tight and not letting anybody in in whatever way, shape or form, therefore you become very sensitive to any kind of criticism. There is a reason for doing that - it draws you together and allows you to create a bit more determination and drive to be successful. You could see England's intensity, their accuracy and their discipline. All the things that have maybe been highlighted over the past nine months as things England have been lacking, there was an abundance of all of it. As much as it is easy to try to pick holes in England because it is England, sometimes you have got to pat people on the back and say they got it right. item.description: Manchester United v Aston Villa FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Roy Keane has launched a scathing assessment of Michael Carrick’s leadership at Manchester United, likening the under-fire manager to a "politician" who avoids giving straight answers. item.title: Fishlock retires after record-breaking career
item.description: Jess Fishlock won more caps and scored more goals for Wales than any other player, male or female [Getty Images] Wales legend Jess Fishlock's playing career is over, after Seattle Reign were beaten 1-0 by Gotham FC in the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) play-off quarter-finals. The 39-year-old midfielder began her career with home town club Cardiff City in 2002. She played in eight different countries and collected Champions League winners medals with FFC Frankfurt and Olympique Lyonnais. Fishlock retired from international football in October 2025 after scoring 48 times in 166 international appearances - both Wales records. She won three NWSL Shields during a 14-season stint with Seattle but announced in April this season would be her last. "I've loved it," said an emotional Fishlock, as she wiped away tears after losing to Gotham on Sunday. "And the truth is I've loved that my last year was with this group, because they have just given me so much, and not just on the field." Fishlock will now be part of Rhian Wilkinson's Wales coaching staff for December's two-leg World Cup play-off against Norway. Wales face Denmark and Italy again on League A return Wales in fight to retain rising female stars Fishlock, who has previously held player-coach roles at Cardiff City ladies and Melbourne Victory, joined Seattle for the inaugural NWSL season in 2013. Reign finished eighth in this year's regular season table to claim the final play-off berth, and they pushed number one seed Gotham close in a game during which Fishlock left the field in the 74th minute. "Two years ago I was just 'I can't work with these kids', as in I'm too old for it, but they have given me just so much joy," added Fishlock. "And obviously the older ones, we've just had to rely on each other so much these last couple of years and it's created deeper relationships within what we've already been doing, and because of that I've seen so much growth on and off the field from this team. "So even today I'm not upset that I'll never play football again - I'm ok with that, I've played enough - but I am devastated that I will not get to spend more time with this group because they will win." Reign defender Sofia Huerta said it had been a privelege to play with Fishlock, who she described as the best player she had ever seen. Julia Zigiotti had already scored goals against Arsenal and Liverpool this season and turned up when her team needed her most at the back post to nod in the only goal of the game . Speaking on the game, Eva Olid explained to the club’s website that Zigiotti’s goal from the bench shows how talented her squad is. The Spaniard explained, “in terms of the squad, I want everyone to know that they have to be competitive.” Olid continued, “today she (Zigiotti) didn’t start, but you could see the reaction – she scored a goal. Then the others always need to think: ‘Oh, next time I can be on the bench [and still make an impact].’ But, if they want to play, they need to have impact.” The boss has already claimed that one of the reasons her side is doing so well in the Players’ Cup, as they sit top of the league phase with four wins from four, is due to their impressive squad depth. Olid continued, “Zigi, today, was excellent when she came in, worked so hard and scored the winning goal again – because against Liverpool she [also scored] the goal. She’s being a key player for us.” She added, “but it’s so good that we have depth. We had a lot of options on the bench today to change the game.
